title: Seazn capture record, v1: POST /api/v1/capture/codes/{code}/records (APPROVED design, owner 2026-10-12)
description: APPROVED design (owner, 2026-10-12; docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-capture-record-upload-design.md), served by POST /api/v1/capture/codes/{code}/records and twinned in apps/web/src/server/api-v1/capture-schemas.ts. The operator's Send record tap (owner rulings R3, R4) posts the phone's scrubbed session record as NDJSON (application/x-ndjson): one JSON object per line, and THIS schema is ONE line. Limits apply to the DECOMPRESSED body: at most 1000 non-empty lines and at most 1 MB (1048576 bytes). Content-Encoding: gzip is accepted; the server inflates at most 1 MB + 1 byte and stops there, so a zip bomb is 413 too_large and is never inflated whole. The keys are capture's modules/capture-engine/src/scrub/allow-list.json (capture 2b4df80): at, kind and level are the line's own; every plain, publicUrl, text and scalars key under its class, a field named like a line key written field_<key>. A bad line is DROPPED and the rest of the record is stored; the body is never refused for a line (owner ruling RL, 2026-10-12). A bad line is one this schema refuses — any other key, a never key included (even masked) and __proto__ included, a value off its key's class, a line that is not a JSON object or not UTF-8 — or one that names any key twice (the server reads the line's TEXT, where a JSON parser keeps only the last value, so no schema can state it: fixture line-server-duplicate-key), or one in which, beyond any shape, any string value is secret-shaped: S1 the Bearer token that sent the record, raw, percent-encoded or form-encoded (the server holds the Bearer; no schema can state it); S2 an RTMP(S) URL that carries a stream key ($defs.secretS2); S3 a streamid or passphrase value, after = or after whitespace ($defs.secretS3); S4 a URL with userinfo ($defs.secretS4); S5 a Bearer credential ($defs.secretS5). A string value that validates against $defs.secretShaped is one of S2–S5. Every rule skips a masked value: a credential the scrub masked in place — *** with no letter or digit after it, whatever punctuation follows — is not secret-shaped, so capture's own scrubbed output (e.g. srt://h:1?passphrase=***&x=1, streamid *** refused, (streamid=***), …/live/***.) is admitted. A kept line is stored as the server re-serialises the object it screened, never as the bytes sent. A bad line is counted twice — in the 201's dropped, and on its own with the stored record so staff can see a scrub leak — and is never stored, logged or echoed. Attribution: the record is the phone's last 1000 lines and can span codes. The server keeps a line only if it belongs to the sending code, and drops every other line before storing: A1 a line whose sid is a uuid is kept iff that session belongs to the sending code (the owner's reading, the spec's Q9: through the session's pairing, so a session with no pairing — an organiser's start with no phone — belongs to no code and its lines are dropped; fixture_stream_sessions.code_id is not used), and a line whose sid is the mask *** is dropped; A2 a line whose sid is null or absent is kept iff it falls inside a pairing window of the sending code: a window opens at a `pair` line whose tokenTag is the tag of a token of the sending code, and runs through the next `unpaired`, `ended`, `pair-refused` or `reset` line (capture's answer to the spec's Q7, as capture corrected it on 2026-10-12: an `engine-error` line closes nothing, because the app also writes one where the pairing goes on, and a fatal error is followed by an `ended` line whose reason is fatal-error), or up to (not including) the next `pair` line or the next line this schema refuses (which may be another code's `pair`, so the window fails closed there), whichever comes first. A secret-shaped line this schema admits is read like any other line and then dropped. A line before the record's first `pair` line is in no window. A dropped line is counted, never stored, logged or echoed. $defs.ok is the 201 answer and $defs.refusal every refusal body (the capture envelope {code, message}: the phone keys on code; message is a developer string the phone never shows). Its sha256 and fixtures are pinned by apps/web/src/server/api-v1/__tests__/capture-contract.test.ts.

at.description: When the line was written: the beat's `at`, byte for byte (R5) — ISO 8601 with any offset, calendar-exact (no 30 February, 29 February only in a leap year), seconds required, a value with no zone refused. The server normalises it to UTC. Capture's writers send Z with milliseconds (IsoTime.utc, Date.toISOString), e.g. 2026-10-11T21:19:03.123Z. NOT epoch milliseconds: the design brief said ms epoch, and capture's writers say otherwise (spec 2026-10-12, §0.1).

kind.description: What the line records: a plain word (capture's modules/capture-engine/src/scrub/allow-list.json, its `kinds`), or the mask *** when capture's scrub masked it. A kind outside capture's list is admitted: the list grows with the app, and a word is not a secret.

level.description: debug, warn or error; ABSENT means info, which capture never writes (CD7). info is admitted when sent, and the mask *** is native's answer to a level it does not vet.

ok.description: 201: the record was received. The bare shape, never an {ok, data} envelope. Owner ruling 2026-10-12: the app shows ONLY the ref ("Sent — ref R-7K2Q") and says nothing about dropped lines; the server still returns dropped, and the app ignores it. kept + dropped is the number of non-empty lines received. dropped counts every line not stored: another code's or an unattributable one (A1, A2), and every bad line (owner ruling RL, 2026-10-12: dropped, not refused). Approved (owner, 2026-10-12): the server records both counts with the record (P5), and a record whose every line was dropped is still 201 (kept 0), stored as counts with no lines (P10).

ref.description: The record's reference, for the operator to read to the organiser: R- and four characters of upper-case Crockford base32 (no I, L, O or U), e.g. R-7K2Q; the server may lengthen it to eight without a new version. Unique among the records still kept (P9).

kept.description: Lines stored: those that belong to the sending code (A1, A2).

dropped.description: Lines not stored: another code's or unattributable (A1, A2), and bad lines — off the allow-list or its class, not a JSON object, not UTF-8, or secret-shaped (owner ruling RL, 2026-10-12). The app ignores it (owner ruling 2026-10-12).

refusal.description: Every refusal: 401 code_ended (a missing, malformed or wrong Bearer, an unknown code, a code that no longer serves a record under the spec's §4 — C1, then 24 h after it last served: one sentence, no oracle), 404 not_a_stream_code (a malformed code), 413 too_large (over 1000 lines or 1 MB decompressed; a new word, approved: Q2), 422 invalid (a body the server cannot read as lines: an unsupported Content-Encoding, a gzip that will not decode, or no non-empty line at all (P10); a bad LINE is never refused, it is dropped — owner ruling RL, 2026-10-12), 429 rate_limited (10 records an hour per code, with Retry-After), 503 unavailable (anything unmapped). Never replaced: a replaced phone may send (R4).

code.description: The machine word the phone keys on.

message.description: A plain English developer string; the phone never shows it. It never quotes a line's value.

secretS2.description: S2: an RTMP(S) URL that carries a stream key — two or more path segments after the host, the last not the mask (*** with no letter or digit after it, so …/live/***. and "…/live/***" pass). Cloudflare's bare ingest URL (rtmps://live.cloudflare.com:443/live/) carries none.

secretS3.description: S3: SRT's credentials, with or without a scheme — a streamid= or passphrase= pair whose value is not the mask (*** with no letter or digit after it, so passphrase=***& and (streamid=***) pass), or the word streamid or passphrase, whitespace, then at least 16 token characters (capture's vector 24, streamid a1b2…90 refused). The mask is no token character, so streamid *** refused passes.

secretS4.description: S4: a URL with userinfo (scheme://user:password@ or scheme://token@) whose password, or whole userinfo, is not exactly ***.

secretS5.description: S5: a Bearer credential — the word Bearer, then at least 16 token characters. The mask is no token character, so `Bearer ***` never matches.

secretShaped.description: A string that is secret-shaped under S2–S5 (S1 needs the Bearer and is the server's alone). The server drops a line in which any string value validates against this (owner ruling RL, 2026-10-12).
